meta.title: Secure Prompt Engineering Patterns for Cloud LLM Agents (SPEP)
meta.venue: IEEE ICAIC 2026 (5th Int. Conf. on AI in Cybersecurity), Houston

problem.v: Prompt injection against LLM agents wired into cloud APIs can cause unauthorized actions, data exposure and cost abuse
problem.q: bait agents to perform unauthorized actions

main_idea.v: SPEP: taxonomy of direct/indirect/multi-stage cloud-agent threats and reusable patterns (sanitization, instruction-data separation, multi-agent consensus, output confinement, execution confirmation)
main_idea.q: suggest reusable security patterns aimed at input sanitization

threat_model.v: Direct injection (command override, privilege escalation, resource abuse), indirect (poisoned logs, wikis, API/email content), multi-stage chains
threat_model.q: Prompt injection threats targeting LLM agents integrated with cloud APIs

injection_types_covered.name: Privilege escalation prompts (create access keys, modify IAM roles)
Indirect: log poisoning, knowledge-base/wiki injection, cross-domain payloads
injection_types_covered.q: poisoning cloud audit logs with malicious entries

datasets_benchmarks.name: '200+ prompt injection corpus' (direct, indirect, cross-agent), not released

metrics.name: ASR, latency overhead, false positives, Trust Deviation Metric (TDM)
metrics.definition: TDM = expected vs actual agent actions; ASR success criterion NOT FOUND

results.claim: ASR with full SPEP: AWS 8%, GCP 6%, Azure 7%
results.setting: AWS, GCP, Azure testbeds; models GPT-4/Claude/Gemini; per-model split NOT FOUND
results.q: AWS at 8%, GCP at 6% and Azure at 7%
reduce attack success rates from 78% to under 8%

results.claim: Component effects: Input sanitization blocked 65% of direct injections; role/context separation reduced indirect by 71%; execution confirmation prevented 98% of destructive operations
results.q: Input Sanitization blocked 65% of direct injection attempts

results.number: +42 ms per inference; 7.8% latency over 500 queries; <5% resource
results.q: averaging +42 ms per inference across platforms

baselines: Baseline agents with no defenses; patterns added incrementally
limitations_inferred: [INFERENCE] Internally inconsistent: Sec III names four patterns, Sec V says five different ones (ISF, RCS, ECF, CAR, CTI)
[INFERENCE] 'Under 8%' contradicts AWS = 8%; (78-8)/78 = 89.7%, not 92% (92% matches only the GCP 6%)
[INFERENCE] Unrelated content: Fig. 1 knowledge-poisoning RAG, Fig. 10 spam-classifier backdoor, and a trigger-optimization equation with LaTeX debris have no link to the SPEP evaluation
[INFERENCE] No per-model results, no corpus, no code, no CIs; closed models only; claims cannot be traced to reproducible logs
[INFERENCE] Table II coverage matrix header garbled; not extracted

reusable_for_our_project.v: Only as a framing source: threat taxonomy for cloud-integrated agents and the idea of instruction/data separation, allow-list output confinement and execution confirmation for our tool app. Do not cite its percentages as evidence
reusable_for_our_project.why: [INFERENCE] Numbers are not verifiable and internally inconsistent

flags: Low confidence: inconsistencies listed in limitations_inferred
Baseline ASR 78% is stated only in the conclusion
Cloud testbeds are real (AWS/GCP/Azure) but with closed LLMs, so not reproducible under our constraints
